lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking

The people of Taif rejected his message and mocked him. One day a mob pelted him with stones and injured him. Despite his injuries, he prayed for them.

Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) was called Al-Saadiq (the truthful) and Al-Amin (the trustworthy) because he always spoke the truth and people trusted him with their belongings.

Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) treated his opponents with patience. He never lost his patience, never scolded his enemies, and always prayed to Allah to guide them towards the right path and forgive them.

Fill in the blanks (from the lesson)

The people of Taif refused to accept Islam.

Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) stayed in Taif for ten days.

  • Sara had an egg for breakfast.
  • Please give me an apple.
  • I saw a small cat in the park.
  • Maria bought an umbrella.

Because he travelled to many lands
Because he was a brave warrior

mcqs.q: What does the title Al-Amin mean?
mcqs.why: Al-Amin means the trustworthy; people trusted him with their belongings because of this quality.

options: They rejected it and mocked him
mcqs.why: The lesson tells us the people of Taif rejected his message and mocked him.

mcqs.why: The fill-in-the-blanks answer in the lesson states that he stayed in Taif for ten days.

options: They pelted him with stones and injured him
mcqs.why: The lesson says a mob pelted him with stones one day and injured him badly.

mcqs.q: How did Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) treat his opponents?
options: He treated them with patience and never scolded them
mcqs.why: The lesson says he treated his opponents with patience, never lost his patience and never scolded his enemies.

options: To guide them to the right path and forgive them

mcqs.why: He always prayed to Allah to guide his enemies towards the right path and to forgive them.

options: Because he was Al-Amin, the trustworthy
mcqs.why: People trusted him with their belongings because he was Al-Amin, the trustworthy one.

I saw a small cat in the park.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Getting Started (discussion)

What values do we need to consider while working in a group? — Cooperation, patience, honesty, respect for others and sharing work fairly.

Why is it important to have patience when working with friends? — Patience keeps the group peaceful, avoids quarrels and helps everyone finish the work together.

What would you do if you were in Azlan's place? — I would apologise to my group members, explain my delay honestly and finish my part of the work on time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a value we need while working in a group?
mcqs.why: The discussion answers list cooperation, patience, honesty, respect for others and sharing work fairly as group values.

mcqs.q: Why is patience important when working with friends?
options: It helps one person do all the work
It keeps the group peaceful and avoids quarrels
mcqs.why: Patience keeps the group peaceful, avoids quarrels and helps everyone finish the work together.

mcqs.q: What would you do if you were in Azlan's place after being late with your work?
options: Apologise, explain the delay honestly and finish my part on time
mcqs.why: The model answer says: apologise to the group members, explain the delay honestly and finish the work on time.

mcqs.q: What does 'sharing work fairly' mean in a group?
options: Dividing the work justly among all members
Giving all work to one member
mcqs.why: Sharing work fairly means every member gets a just share of the work, as the discussion answer states.

mcqs.q: Which quality means telling the group the true reason for a delay?
mcqs.why: Explaining a delay honestly is the quality of honesty listed among the group-work values.

mcqs.q: What can happen in a group when members lose patience?
options: Quarrels can start in the group
mcqs.why: The lesson says patience avoids quarrels, so losing patience can lead to quarrels in the group.

mcqs.q: Cooperation in a group means:
options: Working together and helping one another
mcqs.why: Cooperation, the first value in the lesson's answer, means working together and helping one another.

mcqs.q: How can a member show respect for others in a group?
mcqs.why: Respect for others, one of the listed values, is shown by listening to and valuing their ideas.

mcqs.q: Finishing your part of the group work on time shows that you are:
mcqs.why: The Azlan answer ends with finishing his part of the work on time, which is responsible behaviour.

mcqs.q: A peaceful group is one where members:
mcqs.why: The lesson links peace in a group with patience, honesty, cooperation and fair sharing of work.

lessons.notes_html:
B) Reading and Critical Thinking

The people of Pakistan gave Fatima Jinnah the title of 'Madar-e-Millat' (Mother of the Nation) due to her untiring efforts for Muslim women, especially during the Pakistan Movement. She formed the Women's Relief Committee, which later was renamed as 'All Pakistan Women's Association'.

Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor and nun known as Mother Teresa of Pakistan, devoted her life to fighting leprosy in Pakistan. She travelled to various parts of Pakistan, set up 150 leprosy clinics across the country, and due to her efforts the disease came under control in 1996.

Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa became the pride of Pakistan when she was only nine years old by achieving the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional award. Her representation in prestigious technology events, including the TechEd Developers Conference, made Pakistan proud in the whole world. She flew her first aircraft at the age of ten in the U.A.E.

At the age of nine, Arfa got the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional award.

Fable: 'What Goes Around, Comes Around'

The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread so that he could pull the mouse along to see the wonderful underwater world, because the mouse could not swim. The frog laughed as he thought it would be good fun for him.

The poor mouse was drowned, while the cruel frog frisked about down below, tied to the foot of the mouse. Just then, a hawk saw the mouse and pounced upon it. As he flew away with it, the frog was dragged out of the water too, for he was still tied to the mouse. The hawk said he wanted them both and would eat the frog first, for he liked frog meat even better than mouse meat. In a few moments, the hawk had a good supper, and there was nothing left of either the selfish frog or the poor mouse.

A mouse who lived on land met a frog who lived in water. The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a thread to show him the underwater world. The frog jumped into the pond and swam happily, but the poor mouse drowned. A hawk pounced on the mouse and dragged the frog out too, and ate them both. Moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

My favourite character is the mouse, because he was innocent and trusted his friend, even though the frog deceived him.

The Hare and the Tortoise

Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The hare was very proud of his speed. He used to make fun of the tortoise for being too slow. One day, the tortoise challenged the hare to a race. The hare accepted the challenge. The race started. The hare ran very fast. The tortoise was left much behind. The hare got tired and stopped to have some rest under a tree. He fell asleep. The tortoise passed by him and reached the winning post. The hare woke up and ran as fast as he could. He saw that the tortoise was already there at the winning post. The tortoise had won the race.

A nation's strength is not gold but men. Brave men who work while others sleep, who dare while others fly, who stand fast for truth and honour's sake and suffer long — they build a nation's pillars deep and lift them to the sky.

The message of the poem is that good people are more important than gold and jewels. A nation becomes great and strong through brave, truthful and hardworking people who serve it selflessly.

Education is important because it makes a nation strong by making people learned and skillful. It also makes lives better for those who need to struggle for their survival. Strong nations always work hard for the welfare of society.

lessons.notes_html:
Poem: 'Two Little Kittens'

The kittens began to quarrel because one had a mouse and the other had none, and that was the way the quarrel begun.

The old woman swept the kittens out of the room because they began to quarrel and then to fight.

The kittens learnt that fighting is a bad thing. They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.

Fighting is a bad thing because when we fight with others we often harm ourselves too. The kittens were swept out of the room into the storm and came back wet with snow and as cold as ice. So we should always avoid fighting.

The setting of the poem is a house on a stormy night. The words that helped are: 'One stormy night', 'wet with snow', 'as cold as ice', and 'lie by the fire'.

Fighting is a bad thing because it harms us and others, breaks friendships, and makes us sad. Peace and kindness are better than quarrelling.

The moral of the poem is that fighting is a bad thing, so always try to avoid it. We know this because the kittens realised their mistake and found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.

This poem is about two little kittens. They began to quarrel with each other during a stormy night. One kitten had a mouse but the other kitten had none, so their quarrel began. The old woman became angry and swept them out of her house with her broom. Then, they returned wet and cold. They realised their mistake and felt ashamed. They found that it is better to lie by the fire in the house than to quarrel and fight. They had learnt that fighting is a bad thing, so always try to avoid it.
